thread:
Maya (go-sdk): Heads-up: I found a goroutine/connection leak in the Go generator sample app when callers cancel ctx but don't explicitly Close the stream. Repro is small and scary for long-lived services.
Ravi (eng): oh no. can you paste the minimal repro? We should probably make the sample app defensive by default.
Maya (go-sdk): minimal repro below. Basically: create stream, consume a few events, then cancel ctx. The stream's reader goroutine stays alive because the transport read isn't interrupted reliably.
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 500*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
cli := redwood.NewClient(token)
g := cli.Generator("gpt-mini")
stream, err := g.GenerateStream(ctx, &gen.Request{Prompt: "start"})
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for i := 0; i < 2; i++ { ev := <-stream.Events(); fmt.Println(ev.Text) }
// ctx cancel fires here, but we never call stream.Close()
// process exits later but goroutine still blocks on transport.Read
```
Maya (go-sdk): behavior varies by transport (http2 vs websockets). On http2 the stream's read can block until server EOF; canceling ctx doesn't always interrupt the low-level read.
Lina (runtime): that's tricky. on runtime side we try to send stream end on cancel, but network races happen. We should guarantee client-side API provides a Close/Stop that cancels the transport and drains resources.
Sam (devex): this is an onboarding friction: our current quickstart omits stream.Close in examples. New hires copy/paste and hit leaks after a few minutes of testing. 
Ravi (eng): proposal: make GeneratorStream implement io.Closer in Go and document "defer stream.Close()" in examples. Also add a CloseWithContext(ctx) variant to allow bounded shutdown.
Maya (go-sdk): I prototyped CloseWithContext which cancels internal read and waits up to ctx deadline for background goroutine to exit. Added test that asserts no goroutine leaks via runtime.NumGoroutine check.
Lina (runtime): also consider making GenerateStream return an explicit cancel func: stream, cancel := gen.GenerateStream(ctx, req). That pattern reduces accidental leaks for beginners. But API ergonomics matter.
Sam (devex): for docs: add a short "streams and lifecycle" page in the Go quickstart. Show both patterns: defer stream.Close() and the cancel func pattern. Include a note about network transports and that behavior may differ on local proxies.
Maya (go-sdk): filed draft PR: https://git.redwood/patch/go/stream-close-101 that adds CloseWithContext, example updates, and a sample app called stream-lifecycle. Included a tiny script to assert no leftover goroutines.
Ravi (eng): can we also add a linter rule in sample apps CI to run the leak test on main branches? That will catch regressions.
Docs-Bot: created docs task #452: "quickstart: clarify stream lifecycle and show Close/Cancel patterns"
Sam (devex): tiny UX ask: make the error returned after Close deterministic (e.g., context.Canceled) instead of wrapped transport errors. That makes handling simpler in apps.
Maya (go-sdk): agreed. I'll normalise the returned error to context.Canceled when CloseWithContext was called and timeout occurred.
Lina (runtime): pinging networking to ensure transport-level Read is interruptible on cancel. Filing infra task.
Sam (devex): can someone update the onboarding checklist for new hires to run the stream-lifecycle sample? It helped me understand generator semantics faster.
Ravi (eng): will add to onboarding playbook.
Maya (go-sdk): thanks all — PR has tests and sample README. cc @Sam for docs review.
Sam (devex): review requested. ci/build-bot: please run the leak-suite on the PR.
Docs-Bot: review assigned to Sam.
